summary.short: Amends the Chilean Labour Code to regulate digital service platform companies and their workers, treating those working dependently as employees and setting pay floors, working-time, data, non-discrimination and protection rules for dependent and independent platform workers, from the first day of the sixth month after publication.
summary.long: Law 21.431 amends the Labour Code (Art. 38 and a new Chapter X, Arts. 152 quáter P to 152 quinquies I) to regulate work through digital service platforms. It defines platform service companies and platform workers, and treats a platform worker as dependent when the subordination conditions of Art. 7 are met, and as independent otherwise. Dependent workers' contracts must set out terms such as work location, remuneration method and a complaints channel, and their hourly pay may not fall below a proportion of the minimum monthly wage increased by 20%. Independent workers receive a written contract, a minimum hourly fee on the same basis, a minimum daily disconnection period of twelve continuous hours, 30 days' written notice of termination after six months of continuous service, and social security coverage. Common rules cover information on offered services, access to and portability of personal data, a duty to avoid algorithmic discrimination, safety training and protective equipment, and collective bargaining rights. The Dirección del Trabajo supervises compliance, and fines under Art. 506 are doubled for repeat offences. Transitional provisions give existing companies three years to meet the employer requirement in Art. 19(1) of the Labour Code and require an annual report by the Consejo Superior Laboral for three years.](truncated)

notes: Annotated from the enacted text as published (promulgated 8 March 2022). Only relations and entities were requested; no other Tier A sections were coded. The Código del Trabajo is not in the registry, so its target_instrument_id is empty. Internal Código references (arts. 7, 10, 22, 33, 44, 163, 216, 314, 485, 506) are not coded as relations. Art. 152 quinquies I refers to fines under art. 506 without stating an amount here. Art. 152 quáter Y (independents) and art. 152 quáter V (dependents) both set a minimum hourly floor of the minimum monthly income plus 20 per cent, but state the divisor differently (180 hours; four times the weekly ordinary hours limit of art. 22). The text does not reconcile the two wordings. The transitional provisions (arts. primero and segundo) use dates tied to publication, which are not stated in the text.
